analyst.summary: Crompton's FY26 headline loss (Rs.230.76cr) looks alarming but is a one-off: a Rs.716.04cr non-cash writedown on the Butterfly Gandhimathi kitchen-appliances unit, the SECOND such impairment on that 2022 acquisition (the first was ~Rs.692cr in FY24). Strip that out and the underlying business improved through the year - Q4 delivered the highest quarterly operating profit on record, helped by the GST rate cuts on durables (effective Sep-2025) and price hikes recovering margin from commodity cost pressure. The balance sheet is clean (near-zero debt, strong interest cover) and the dividend was maintained. The concern is less about this quarter and more about a pattern: management has now destroyed roughly Rs.1,400cr of capital on one acquisition twice, growth has been mid-single-digit on a trailing basis, and the stock's forward valuation (~27.5x) already assumes a good deal of the hoped-for recovery holds up. We are holding, not selling, and the next real test is the Q1 FY27 result due around 6-Aug-2026.
